title: Rezk nerve comparison of complete Segal spaces and infinity categories
statement:
Use the spaces, infinity categories and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with universes as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Write $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ for the infinity category of small infinity categories and $\mathrm{CSS}_\infty$ for the full infinity subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Spc})$ on Rezk-complete Segal spaces, with the following conventions. A Segal space is a simplicial small space $Z$ for which the canonical maps $Z_n\to Z_1\times_{Z_0}\cdots\times_{Z_0}Z_1$ induced by consecutive edges $\{i-1,i\}\hookrightarrow[n]$ are equivalences for every $n\ge2$; all fiber products are homotopy fiber products. The identities and composition are induced by the simplicial degeneracies and these Segal maps. Let $Z_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq Z_1$ be the union of components whose arrows are invertible in the resulting homotopy category (a two-sided inverse is required, up to the composition homotopies). Rezk completeness means that the identity-arrow degeneracy $s_0:Z_0\to Z_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is an equivalence. For a small infinity category $C$, let
$$R(C)_n=\operatorname{Fun}([n],C)^\simeq,$$
where $[n]$ is the category $0\to\cdots\to n$, viewed as an infinity category, and $(-)^\simeq$ is the maximal subgroupoid (the space of objects and equivalences). Precomposition makes $R(C)$ a simplicial space. This construction defines an equivalence of infinity categories $R:\mathrm{Cat}_\infty\simeq\mathrm{CSS}_\infty$. For objects $x,y$ of $C$, the homotopy fiber at $(x,y)$ of $R(C)_1\to R(C)_0\times R(C)_0$ is naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_C(x,y)$. The equivalence $R$ and this mapping-space identification are natural in $C$ as coherent functors of infinity categories. In particular, for every small infinity category $K$, postcomposition with $R$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathrm{CSS}_\infty)$.

source.place: Joyal–Tierney, Quasi-categories vs Segal spaces, section 4, Proposition 4.9, Proposition 4.10 and Theorem 4.11; the construction Gamma(C)_n=J(C^{Delta[n]}). Read online; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Represent $C$ by a small quasicategory $Q$ and put $\Gamma(Q)_{p,q}=C(Q)_{p,q}$ of [lem-coef-quasicategory-classification-realization]. Its stated equality $C(Q)_{p,\bullet}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^p,Q)^\simeq$ identifies it with the formula for $R(C)$, including all simplicial operators. The same cited statement gives the homotopy Segal condition. This is the ordinal-arrow construction, not $\operatorname{Map}(E^p,Q)$ for the indiscrete equivalence algebroids.

source.place: Proposition 4.9 and the first part of Proposition 4.10.

proof.text: The matching map for $\Gamma(Q)$ in degree $p$ is the restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^p,Q)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^p,Q)^\simeq$. Indeed a compatible collection of boundary-face simplices is exactly a map from the boundary, and the condition that each vertical edge be an equivalence is tested on its vertices. Apply the Kan restriction-fibration assertion of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] to $(\partial\Delta^p)^\flat\hookrightarrow(\Delta^p)^\flat$ and $Q^\natural$. Thus $\Gamma(Q)$ is vertically Reedy fibrant, including degree zero, where the restriction is $Q^\simeq\to *$.

By [lem-coef-quasicategory-classification-realization], the endpoint projection on $\Gamma(Q)_1$ is a Kan fibration with strict fiber $U_Q(x,y)$, also modeling its homotopy fiber. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], the specified right-pinch map $\operatorname{Map}_Q(x,y)\to U_Q(x,y)$ is a natural homotopy equivalence. These give the required equivalence of homotopy fibers with the right-pinched mapping-space convention fixed in the statement. On vertices this identifies an arrow with that same edge of $Q$; the long edge of a $2$-simplex computes composition in both homotopy categories. Consequently invertibility in $h\Gamma(Q)$ is precisely invertibility of the corresponding edge of $Q$.

source.place: Section 1, arrow-space convention; mapping-space identification via the specified pinch comparison.

proof.text: Let $A$ be the full subquasicategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Q)$ on equivalence edges of $Q$. The preceding step identifies $\Gamma(Q)_{\mathrm{eq}}$ with $A^\simeq$: equivalence of arrows in the functor category is componentwise by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so the condition on its objects selects exactly the indicated components of the core. Evaluation at the source is an inverse to the constant-arrow map $Q\to A$ up to a specified natural equivalence. The composite evaluation after constant arrow is the identity. For the other composite, the monotone map $[1]\times[1]\to[1]$, $(t,s)\mapsto\min(t,s)$, supplies the transformation from the constant source arrow to the original arrow $f$. Its endpoint components are $1_x$ and $f$, both equivalences. The componentwise criterion makes this transformation an equivalence. Its restriction to cores is a simplicial homotopy, since its edges in the transformation direction are equivalences; reversing its equivalence gives the inverse homotopy. Hence $s_0:Q^\simeq\to\Gamma(Q)_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is an equivalence. Together with the preceding two steps, this makes $\Gamma(Q)$ fibrant in the Rezk structure of [lem-coef-rezk-local-model].

source.place: Proposition 4.10, completeness; explicit identity-arrow deformation retraction replacing an appeal to algebroid completion.

proof.text: Put $(p^*A)_{p,q}=A_p$ and $i^*Z=Z_{\bullet,0}$. A map $p^*A\to Z$ is determined by its degree-zero vertical part, because its value on every vertical simplex must be the degeneracy of that value. This gives $p^*\dashv i^*$. Taking $j:\varnothing\to\Delta^0$ in the box pushout-product theorem of [lem-coef-rezk-local-model] shows that $p^*$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations from the Joyal structure. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to obtain the derived adjunction, with coherent unit and counit. All source objects are cofibrant since cofibrations are monomorphisms in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure].

source.place: Proposition 4.6 and beginning of Proposition 4.7; derived adjunction with coherent naturality.

proof.text: The row $\Gamma(Q)_{\bullet,q}$ is the full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\Delta^q,Q)$. Degree by degree, the equality says that a map $\Delta^p\times\Delta^q\to Q$ has equivalence edges in each vertical $\Delta^q$ exactly when all of its $p$-vertices are such functors; the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] gives the equivalent core condition. The constant-functor map $Q\to\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\Delta^q,Q)$ has inverse evaluation at $0$ up to a coherent natural equivalence. In detail the monotone map $[q]\times[1]\to[q]$ sending $(t,0)$ to $0$ and $(t,1)$ to $t$ gives a transformation from the constant functor at $F(0)$ to $F$. Each component is $F(0\to t)$ and is invertible by the definition of this full subcategory. The componentwise criterion therefore makes it an equivalence. Whiskering this quasi-inverse and its inverse transformations with functors to any test quasicategory gives inverse equivalences on the testing homotopy categories in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], so each row map is a categorical equivalence. Thus the natural map $a_Q:p^*Q\to\Gamma(Q)$ is a Rezk weak equivalence by [lem-coef-segal-categorical-constancy]. Its first row is exactly $1_Q$.

source.place: Propositions 4.9-4.10, including the row calculation $\Gamma(Q)_{\bullet,q}=Q^{(\Delta^q)}$ and the constant-row replacement map.

proof.text: For a Rezk-fibrant $Z$, [lem-coef-segal-categorical-constancy] says that $i^*Z$ is a quasicategory and every row of the ordinary counit $\epsilon_Z:p^*i^*Z\to Z$ is a categorical equivalence: its row of degree $q$ is exactly the degeneracy $Z_{\bullet,0}\to Z_{\bullet,q}$. The same node makes $\epsilon_Z$ a Rezk weak equivalence. Since $i^*Z$ is cofibrant and $Z$ is fibrant, this ordinary counit represents the derived counit of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. For a fibrant Joyal object $Q$, use the Rezk weak equivalence $a_Q$ to the Rezk-fibrant $\Gamma(Q)$ as its fibrant replacement after $p^*$. The derived unit is then represented by $Q\to i^*\Gamma(Q)$, which is $1_Q$ by the preceding step. Every Joyal object is weakly equivalent to a fibrant one. Hence both derived unit and derived counit are equivalences, and the derived functors are mutually inverse as infinity functors.

source.place: Proofs of Proposition 4.7 and Theorem 4.11; explicit unit and counit calculation.

proof.text: The Quillen equivalence in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], together with the coherent derived-adjunction theorem already used, identifies the Joyal localization with the Bergner localization; the same coherent-nerve statement identifies the latter with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Also, [lem-coef-rezk-local-model] identifies the Rezk homotopy theory with the full subcategory $\mathrm{CSS}_\infty$ specified in the item, retaining coherent mapping spaces. Thus the left derived functor in the preceding step is computed on every $Q$ by $\Gamma(Q)$ and is precisely $R$. For a categorical equivalence $f:Q\to Q^\prime$, $p^*f$ is a Rezk weak equivalence by the derived-adjunction preservation assertion, since every source object is cofibrant. The naturality square for $a$ and two-out-of-three therefore make $\Gamma(f)$ a Rezk weak equivalence as well. The natural maps $a_Q$ identify these functors after localization; this is an identification of coherent functors, because the derived-adjunction node supplies coherent localization and natural transformations, not just an equivalence of homotopy categories. The mapping-fiber comparison in step 3 is natural under every functor carrying the endpoints, as stated in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] and the classification-diagram node. Restriction along simplicial operators and postcomposition are the same maps throughout, so these comparisons also give the claimed coherent naturality.

source.place: Theorem 4.11, interpreted in homotopy coherent localizations; Proposition 4.9 identifies the actual derived functor.

proof.text: Let $S$ be the coherent inverse to $R$ obtained from the derived right adjoint. For any small $K$, postcomposition gives $R_*$ and $S_*$. Whiskering the two coherent natural equivalences $SR\simeq1$ and $RS\simeq1$ with a $K$-diagram gives natural transformations $S_*R_*\simeq1$ and $R_*S_*\simeq1$. Their components are equivalences, so [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes them equivalences in the functor infinity categories. These are the inverse data for the asserted equivalence on $\operatorname{Fun}(K,-)$. This argument includes $K=\varnothing$.

source.place: Formal consequence of Theorem 4.11, with the coherent derived units and counits whiskered explicitly; not a separate quoted paragraph in the source.

Item statement: unchanged and true. Edge cases ∅, N[1] (fiber 0→1 is a point, 1→0 empty) and BG all behave as stated.

Steps 1–9 hold:
- Step 1: C(Q)_{p,•}=Fun(Δ^p,Q)^≃ matches R, and the homotopy Segal property comes from the classification node.
- Step 2: the matching object is Map^♯((∂Δ^p)^♭,Q^♮), and restriction is a Kan fibration by the marked-anodyne node; at p=0, M_0=*.
- Step 3: the strict fiber U_Q is equivalent to the pinched Map by the pinch node, so hΓ(Q)≅hQ.
- Step 4: the min(t,s) transformation has components 1_x and f and restricts to cores, so s_0 is a homotopy equivalence and Γ(Q) is complete.
- Step 5: p^*A=A⊠Δ^0, and the box theorem with j=∅→Δ^0 makes p^* left Quillen.
- Step 6: the map (t,0)↦0, (t,1)↦t is monotone with components F(0→t) invertible, so the rows are categorical equivalences and a_Q is a Rezk equivalence whose first row is 1_Q.
- Step 7: the counit rows are degeneracies, handled by the constancy clause under fibrancy; the derived unit is i^*a_Q=1_Q.
- Step 8: the coherent-nerve node identifies the Joyal localization with Cat_∞, the Rezk node identifies the Rezk localization with CSS_∞, and the a-square with 2-out-of-3 finishes.
- Step 9: elementary whiskering.

proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle (the item's 251-node dependency closure does not contain it).

lem-coef-rezk-local-model: Bousfield-localized vertical Reedy structure (cofibrations are monomorphisms, fibrant objects are Reedy-fibrant complete Segal spaces, weak equivalences detected by vertical Map_ss), the ∞-localization identified with complete Segal objects, and the mixed Joyal/Kan box theorem. All true; tested on the spine with ∅→Δ^0, on Δ^0⊠(weak equivalence), and on M_0=*. Not a duplicate of the generic Bousfield or Reedy nodes, the DK-levelwise, explicit-completion or inverse-evaluation nodes, or the algebroid Segal-localization nodes.

lem-coef-segal-categorical-constancy: rows are quasicategories with categorical-equivalence degeneracies (true via the vertical cotensor), and rowwise categorical equivalence implies Rezk equivalence for arbitrary source and target (true via the coend X≅∫^q X_{•,q}⊠Δ^q and the box theorem). The noncomplete walking-isomorphism nerve has constant rows; this is consistent because the converse is not claimed.

Neither new node restates a clause of the item, both are statement-only, and the Mathlib search records cover all three required kinds.
